summary: The Obsidian vault records a narrative that pivoted four times in roughly ten days. (1) Pre-June baseline: the rejected ECCV submission led with directed coverage + SDF-Fractal3D as the main novelty. (2) The 2026-05-28/06-05 reframe (Overview.md, Paper 2 - Outline, codex_analysis 06-07): headline = "motion-domain cross-distance predicts within-context transfer; appearance (DINO) does not," with perf = L + g, three CV regimes (LOTO/LOBO/JOINT), motion_sym (FID+SW2+MMD) recommended as the headline family, the closed interventional loop (KITTI predicted +0.93 vs actual +0.87, FlyingThings negative control) and robustness battery as the strength. The Advisor Audit (06-04) blessed exactly this version ("Project 2 scientific core ~80-90% complete, manuscript ~35-45%"), demanded the causal/SDF/directed-coverage claims be retired, and ordered a scope freeze for the June-22 dissertation draft. (3) The 06-08/09 intervention-grid phase (Session note, ACCV Camera-Ready Assessment 06-09): the 13-cell from-scratch grid opened dynamic range and tempted a "structure ≫ diversity" spine swap, but the assessment ruled the prediction-spine version "the only one writable today" and flagged single-seed Tier-2 claims, the dead "appearance nearly free (−0.37)" framing (corrected to −2.74), and stale-number inconsistencies. (4) The 06-09/10 Regime-Direction Law (Regime-Direction Law note, Briefing v2, Outline v2, Results Tables, Kitchen Sink): the latest written framing — WHICH direction of directed motion coverage predicts transfer flips with training regime (scratch = precision-bound by off-target mass d(T→B); pretrained = recall-bound by missing support d(B→T)), flip statistic +0.899, exact permutation p=0.0286 (RAFT excluded) / 0.0079 (RAFT as scratch), no flip in DINO space; a fit-free if-statement rule reaches ρ≈0.50-0.51 on all three splits (~the reproducibility ceiling), and a pre-registered out-of-sample test on the 13-cell Kubric grid PASSED (FF arm matched direction +0.656 vs sym −0.011 vs mismatched −0.261). This explicitly inverts the 06-05 framing: symmetric metrics, formerly the recommended headline, become "the direction-blind hedge — decent everywhere, best nowhere," the fitted ridge is demoted to an ablation, and the original ECCV directed-coverage idea is rehabilitated ("washed out only because pooling cancels the two directions"). (5) A still-later reframe lives only in auto-memory (two_cost_model.md, "Round 6, 2026-06-10 late"): scratch pays BOTH costs (utility = dtb+dbt, i.e. sym = total cost) while pretrained pays dbt only; the −0.35 anti-correlation of the two directions is load-bearing; coefficient-ratio claims are normalization-fragile; the old consensus fractions 0.79-0.81 are from a stale CONSENSUS_RULE generation (current CONSENSUS_POLICY 0.73-0.76). Cross-cutting: on 2026-06-10 Middlebury was EXCLUDED everywhere (confirmed eval bug, pretrained pinned ~52.6 PCK; 9 benchmarks, 1,458 cells; the §7.1 closed-loop Middlebury row is void) — yet same-day documents are not fully reconciled (Results Tables T7 still counts Middlebury in the OOS "ALL FOUR benchmarks" PASS, and the law's per-variant table appears in two slightly different numeric generations). Next Steps (last updated 06-08, so partially stale) lists the learned A/B/C embedder build, L-anchor refits, anchor convergence runs, 5 missing feature subsets, architecture-grid ceiling refresh (GLU-Net in flight, FlowFormer untested with three pre-registered predictions), and fenced post-June-22 generator work.
